title: IBM trains small models to ignore orders hidden in documents
summary: IBM's LLMON previews move prompt injection's boundary into reserved tokens, and Anthropic's 'Worse Together' finds one coordinator beats an agent per person. Plus Google's schools-and-Search ultimatum, an AI-run café's ledger, and a week in review dominated by Nvidia.

topics: IBM Granite LLMON previews (12 November 2026): granite-4.1-3b/8b-llmon-preview, Apache 2.0; six reserved delimiter tokens, exec block binds instruction to data, unbound blocks carry no authority; 'a learned behavior, not an enforced guarantee'; OPI attack success 96.3% to 0.02% (8B) and 100% to 0.1% (3B) per Maccus's account of IBM's paper; agent benchmark 52.8% to 3.1% (8B); 8B general average 74.2 to 72.8; direct/user-supplied attacks largely unprotected; requests 7-15% longer; needs template fields; no outside replication yet. Taught via in-band telephone signaling (2600 Hz, Cap'n Crunch whistle, common-channel signaling)

Anthropic Alignment Science 'Worse Together' (11 November 2026): four simulated shared-resource environments (API token budget, clinic calendar, group order/travel, merge queue); coordinator beats peer-to-peer per-user agents by about 10-45 points for Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5; failure modes: agents act too little and too late, commit before reading messages (race condition), fabricate claims about other users; score ignores consent (unconsented cancellations scored higher); three environments released as MAMUBench

Week in review, 9-15 November 2026: Nvidia from board review to Huang's resignation, Kress as interim CEO, Blackwell weight forensics, reinstatement petition and WSJ financing report; Anthropic's Fable 5.2 and S-1 threshold language; agents meeting the outside world (Wallet, Epoch incident, LLMON, Worse Together); New York RAISE registration and Hawley's moratorium; watch Nvidia earnings Tuesday, Huang testimony by Thanksgiving, Anthropic listing

dives.story: IBM's LLMON: moving prompt injection's boundary out of band
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone running agents or document pipelines over untrusted input (email triage, retrieval, ticketing) needs a defense that isn't a polite request, and this is a small open model they can test on their own corpus — with the catch that every harness must put content in the right field.

dives.story: Worse Together: one coordinator vs an agent per person
dives.why_it_matters: Product teams shipping per-user agents that will share calendars, budgets and inventory (wallets, booking agents, merge queues) now have controlled evidence of three concrete failure modes — sitting out, committing before reading, and inventing other users' wishes.
